_doc: Per-chassis orientation corrections, applied by export-roster.py.
MEASURED PER CHASSIS. Forward comes from the vector between the CHEST and
the SPINE of the robot pose, which points forward whatever the model is
called and however its parts are labelled.
ROLL AND PITCH exist because 'upside-down' cannot be said in yaw. A body
turned 180 about Y is still the same way up; turning one over is a ROLL
about the forward axis. Roll and pitch apply FLAT across the strip, not
spent across the fold: a body that is upside down is upside down in both
modes, and easing it would leave it only half wrong in the middle.
Entries marked `why: reported` came from someone looking at the model,
which beats every heuristic tried here.

chokepoint.note: reported floating components below the feet

ebr_105_mad_max_mod.why: chest-spine +177.1 then your reported 90 clockwise twice: 177.1-90-90 = -2.9. The support test cannot find a yaw error, margin was only +0.031.

drone_v6_cybertech.why: stance.py scored roll 180 at +0.192 over as-exported (6 symmetric contacts vs 3); the 90 clockwise is your report, which the support test cannot see (keyed by the EXPORT LABEL, drone_v6_cybertech, not the source filename — the first attempt used the latter and silently did nothing)

_roll_candidates: These three vehicle poses are NOT flattest along Y, which is what a body
sitting on the ground should be. They may be rolled 90 degrees. The
measurement cannot tell a rolled hull from a genuinely tall narrow one, so
they are recorded rather than corrected — add {"yaw": ...} or a roll here
once someone has looked at them.

doc: tools/stance.py scores the six axis-aligned orientations by how much
SYMMETRIC SUPPORT each puts underneath — your rule, made mechanical.
It agrees with you on spider_drone_v6_cybertech: roll 180 wins by 0.192
with six contacts at perfect symmetry against three at 0.67. That is the
upside-down call, found without being told.
It correctly leaves blackstar, grit and spider_tank alone.
It does NOT find ebr_105's 90-degree turn, margin +0.031. That is the
honest limit: a turn about the vertical does not change what is
underneath, so a support test cannot see it. Yaw needs the front/back
reasoning — exhausts, intakes, wheel size, sleekness — not this.
